The seat belt that saves lives began with an ejection seat engineer. In Sweden in 1958, Nils Bohlin, who had built ejection seats for pilots at Saab, joined Volvo as a safety engineer.

Waist-only belts left heads hitting the dash and the wheel, and many people did not wear them. Bohlin spent almost a year on a belt that held the chest and the hips, easy to fasten and easy to release. In 1959 the first Volvos were sold with it, and Volvo let every other car maker use the design for free. Germany's patent office named it 1 of its 8 most important patents in 100 years. In the United States it saves an estimated 15,000 lives a year, and Germany required it on every seat in 2004.

Builders wanted. The Ad Astra Fellowship: 12 months, a room, food, the labs, the machine shop and the compute at $0, a company in your name from day 1. 1 written application, no credentials needed. Apply at joinadastra.com
